hypothesis: The ALU B-operand select is decoded with inverted/incorrect polarity (or the mux in EX is wired opposite to the intended id_ex_alu_b_sel semantics), so R-type ALU instructions use id_ex_imm (usually zero) instead of id_ex_rs2_data, while I-type/U-type instructions use stale/garbage rs2 data instead of the immediate. This single operand-selection defect explains the majority of mismatches: t05_forward `add x2,x1,x2` becomes x1+0 = 0x5 instead of 0xf; t02 R-type results collapse to the rs1 operand or zero (x4 0xb->0x3 for OR with 0, x18 0->1 for XOR with 0, x14/x20/x24 lose the second operand); t03 ADDI uses a garbage rs2 value instead of the sign-extended immediate, yielding 0x000007fe instead of 0xfffff7ff; t04 LUI/AUIPC use rs2 instead of the U-immediate, yielding 0 for x1/x6. The same wrong B operand also corrupts branch comparison operands and load/store address generation, which is why bench_ooo_overlap64 scans with wrong dmem addresses and never reaches its ECALL, so halted times out. The immediate generator and writeback/regfile paths are not the primary cause because LUI and dependent R-type operations both fail even though they use different immediate/commit paths.
constraints: Do not change top-level rv32i5 port names or widths.
Preserve the frozen stage interfaces and valid semantics; bubbles/flushes remain valid-bit clears, not data muxing.
id_ex_alu_b_sel polarity must be consistent between id_stage decode and ex_stage ALU mux: R-type selects rs2_data, I-type/U-type/LUI/AUIPC/jump/branch/load/store address select the correct immediate.
Keep forwarding_unit behavior unchanged: EX/MEM -> EX has priority over MEM/WB -> EX, and x0 is never forwarded.
Do not add stalls beyond load-use; single-cycle imem/dmem response must remain same-cycle.
Preserve synchronous active-low reset and keep dmem_valid low during reset and after halted.
Only WB may set halted/exit_code for a committed ECALL; PC fetch freezes after halt.
verification_targets: bench_ooo_overlap64 must assert halted before max_cycles with exit_code=0 and no timeout.
All previously listed t02_alu_r/t03_alu_imm/t04_upper/t05_forward failed checks must flip to pass, with no new stalls beyond allowed load-use.
rejected_hypotheses: Round 1: spurious EX redirect for non-control instructions; reject because the same ALU-register and upper-immediate failures persist and the operand-selection defect directly explains them.

Round 2: immediate generator mis-decoding I-type/U-type immediates; reject because even after immediate generation was addressed, LUI and R-type dependent results still fail in the same pattern, indicating wrong immediate-vs-rs2 selection r

Round 3: WB-stage/regfile commit-path corruption; reject because the observed wrong values preserve correct destination registers and are explainable by ALU operand selection, including t05_forward which has no writeback-path ambiguity.
Purely missing forwarding-unit path; reject because t04 LUI/AUIPC have no source-register dependency and still fail, so the common cause is ALU B-operand selection, not only EX/MEM forwarding.
